title: Inversion
coreMove: Work backward from failure and remove the causes before chasing success directly.
sourcePressure: The official article frames inversion as solving problems backward, avoiding stupidity rather than chasing brilliance directly, and asking what would cause failure, error, or ruin.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says be pessimistic or make a generic risk list.

sourceAnchors.name: avoiding stupidity
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen support frames inversion as avoiding stupidity rather than chasing brilliance directly
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Sometimes the smartest move is not adding brilliance; it is removing the thing that would make success impossible.

sourceAnchors.name: failure, error, or ruin
sourceAnchors.detail: the model asks what would cause failure, error, or ruin, then works backward from that answer
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Start with the ruined version and the cause list gets sharper.

counterintuition: risk management is the whole job

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a race director preparing a high-altitude trail event
exampleSpecs.stakes: one preventable route or hydration failure could injure runners
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anna writes the headline she never wants to read, then removes the three causes most likely to put a runner in that story
exampleSpecs.firstImage: orange course flags snapping above a rocky switchback

exampleSpecs.audience: an airline station manager opening a new baggage belt
exampleSpecs.stakes: opening weekend could bury the station in delayed bags
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anders imagines the belt jammed at midnight and removes the scanner handoff failure before praising the new system
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rubber belt smell rising from a silent baggage carousel

exampleSpecs.audience: a chef opening a raw-bar special
exampleSpecs.stakes: one missed cold-chain step could harm guests and close the restaurant
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Pablo asks what would have to go wrong for the raw bar to make guests sick, then deletes the weak ice-bin handoff from the service plan
exampleSpecs.firstImage: crushed ice melting around oyster tags

exampleSpecs.audience: a documentary producer with a three-day remote shoot
exampleSpecs.stakes: lost footage cannot be recreated once the crew leaves
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rita imagines landing home with no usable footage and builds the backup ritual backward from that loss
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two memory cards taped to the inside of a field notebook

exampleSpecs.audience: a transit planner adjusting winter ferry service
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed connection could strand shift workers after the last bus
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Nicole start with the stranded-passenger outcome and remove the timetable gap that would create it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dark ferry terminal with the last bus pulling away

exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer marshal planning a street festival entrance
exampleSpecs.stakes: a crowd pinch could turn a family event unsafe
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Martin asks what would cause a crush at the entrance and moves the ticket scan away from the narrow gate before opening
exampleSpecs.firstImage: temporary fencing leaning beside a painted curb

skillTargets: work backward from a concrete failure
choose prevention over more motivational upside

tryThisNowSpec: Write one failure headline for a current plan. Under it, list three causes, then remove or reduce one before doing anything else.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
